n_p01_1.text: 1.1 · Release day: Settings › Pricing opens on Tiers. On release day only Default exists. Every customer is on Default, so no price changes until the client sets up tiers.

n_p01_2.text: 1.2 · Release day: Matrices tab. Today's matrices come across as they are, each with only its Default column.

n_p01_4.text: 1.4 · Result: Opening a matrix shows today's rules as the Default column. Nothing else to set up.

n_p02_1.text: 2.1 · Today: the Pricing page. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p02_2.text: 2.2 · Tiers list. Settings › Pricing › Tiers. Active tiers by number, then archived ones. Default has no badge: its name says it.

n_p02_3.text: 2.3 · Hover the # info icon. The tooltip explains the tier order. Numbers are plain text under the #.

n_p02_4.text: 2.4 · Click the three-dot menu beside New Tier. The list-level menu holds Audit Log.

n_p02_6.text: 2.6 · Result: "Audit Log: Tiers": every tier's changes, newest first. (Also Story 19.)

n_p02_7.text: 2.7 · Click a tier's three-dot menu (never used). Tier 5 has priced nothing: Audit Log, Archive, Delete.

n_p02_8.text: 2.8 · Hover the greyed Delete. A tier that open work orders, estimates or Part Sales use, or that priced saved lines, can't be deleted. Hovering Delete gives the reason.

n_p02_9.text: 2.9 · The last row's menu opens upward. Fleet Old is the last row, so its menu opens upward and stays in view. (Also Story 19.)

n_p02_11.text: 2.11 · Result: The new tier's page opens, no dialog, with the cursor in the name and Cancel / Create Tier. It will be the last tier.

n_p02_12.text: 2.12 · Click Create Tier with no name. A name is required.

n_p02_13.text: 2.13 · Type a name another tier uses. Names are unique among active and archived tiers, ignoring case.

n_p02_14.text: 2.14 · Type an archived tier's name. The archived tier must be renamed first.

n_p02_15.text: 2.15 · Type a name the reports use. "Manual is used by the reports. Choose another name." Manual, Fixed price, Fixed line total and Before tiers are reserved, in any letter case; the message names the reserved name as written.

n_p02_16.text: 2.16 · Type "Fleet Plus" and click Create Tier.

n_p02_17.text: 2.17 · Result: The tier is created and its page stays open. It prices the same as the tier before it until its rules are set.

n_p02_18.text: 2.18 · Archive a tier that has customers.

n_p02_19.text: 2.19 · Click "Remove Customers" in the blocked dialog.

n_p02_20.text: 2.20 · Result: Manage Customers opens on the Remove tab, so the customers can be taken off and the tier archived.

n_p02_21.text: 2.21 · Archive a tier with no customers.

n_p02_22.text: 2.22 · Result: The dialog lists, one per line, every tier that follows it through Same as previous tier.

n_p02_24.text: 2.24 · Result: Tier 5 moves to the archived rows; the tiers after it move up one number.

n_p02_25.text: 2.25 · An archived tier's menu. Reactivate puts it back as the last tier.

n_p02_27.text: 2.27 · Result: No confirmation. Tier 5 comes back as the last tier.

n_p02_28.text: 2.28 · Delete a tier that priced nothing.

n_p02_29.text: 2.29 · Click Delete. This can't be undone.

n_p02_30.text: 2.30 · Result: The tier and its column in every matrix are gone.

t_p02_2.text: Archive, reactivate or delete a tier  (2.18–2.30)

n_p02_32.text: 2.32 · Result: The tier's page opens on Pricing: every matrix and how it prices this tier, in the grid's words.

n_p02_33.text: 2.33 · Point at the name. The rename pencil shows while the pointer is over the name (always on touch screens).

n_p02_35.text: 2.35 · Result: The name is edited in place. Enter or clicking away saves; Esc cancels.

n_p02_36.text: 2.36 · Type a taken name and press Enter. Same name rules as New Tier; nothing is saved.

n_p02_37.text: 2.37 · Type "Fleet" and press Enter. Saved at once. Lines and reports show the new name.

n_p02_38.text: 2.38 · Click the page's three-dot menu. Audit Log, Archive, and Delete (greyed when the tier priced lines).

n_p02_40.text: 2.40 · Result: "Audit Log: Tier 2": Event, User, Details (old → new), Date, Time. (Also Story 19.)

n_p02_42.text: 2.42 · Result: Default is priced by each matrix's Default column, so its page has no checkboxes and no Set Rule.

n_p02_44.text: 2.44 · Result: Archived shows as plain text. It can be renamed and repriced but takes no customers.

n_p02_45.text: 2.45 · Click a matrix on the tier's page.

n_p02_46.text: 2.46 · Result: The matrix opens in edit with Tier 2's column in view; the breadcrumb leads back to the tier.

n_p02_47.text: 2.47 · Check a matrix. The bulk bar appears at the top of the list: count, "Set Tier 2 to", rule, value, Set Rule, clear.

n_p02_48.text: 2.48 · Click select-all. Every matrix, Active and Inactive, is checked.

n_p02_49.text: 2.49 · Uncheck two. The header checkbox shows partly checked.

n_p02_50.text: 2.50 · Type 35. The rule starts on % Off. The other types are in the same picker, grouped as in the grid: Off default price (% Off, $ Off), From cost (+ $, Markup %, Margin %).

n_p02_51.text: 2.51 · Click Set Rule with no value. Blocked, with the message by the bar.

n_p02_52.text: 2.52 · Pick Margin %, type 120, click Set Rule. "Enter a margin from 0 to 99.99"; nothing changes.

n_p02_53.text: 2.53 · Click Set Rule (every matrix checked). "in all <n> matrices" only when every matrix is checked; inactive ones are counted.

n_p02_54.text: 2.54 · Click Set Rule (some checked). Only the checked matrices change.

n_p02_55.text: 2.55 · Click Set Rule in the dialog.

n_p02_56.text: 2.56 · Result: The checks clear. The toast stays 20 seconds, pauses while pointed at, and has Undo.

n_p02_58.text: 2.58 · Result: Exactly what the tier had comes back.

n_p02_59.text: 2.59 · Set a rule it already has.

n_p02_60.text: 2.60 · Result: Nothing is asked; a toast says so.

t_p02_4.text: Set one rule for a tier  (2.47–2.60)

n_p03_2.text: 3.2 · Result: The matrix page: Categories, Work Order / Part Sale tabs, the tier grid (Default and every active tier) and the Price Part Simulator.

n_p03_3.text: 3.3 · Point at the name. The rename pencil shows on hover; the name is renamed in place.

n_p03_5.text: 3.5 · Result: Enter or clicking away saves at once; Esc cancels.

n_p03_6.text: 3.6 · Click the page's three-dot menu. Audit Log for this matrix.

n_p03_8.text: 3.8 · Result: Newest first: each save, then every rule it changed. (Also Story 19.)

n_p03_10.text: 3.10 · Result: No badge on the page; the reason shows as plain text.

n_p03_11.text: 3.11 · Save a matrix that prices one category.

n_p03_12.text: 3.12 · Result: Saved without asking; a toast confirms.

n_p03_13.text: 3.13 · Save a matrix that prices several categories. "Change Prices in <n> Categories?" lists every category, one per line: Cancel / Change All.

n_p03_14.text: 3.14 · Save the General Matrix. It confirms, naming the categories without a matrix of their own.

n_p03_15.text: 3.15 · Type 120 in a % Off column and click Save. The % Off message; Save is blocked.

n_p03_16.text: 3.16 · Change a value, then click the Part Sale Matrix tab. "Discard these changes?" Each tab has its own Edit, Save and Cancel. Keep Editing stays; Discard Changes opens the Part Sale Matrix tab.

n_p03_17.text: 3.17 · Click the Part Sale Matrix tab (off). Part Sales use the work order prices until separate Part Sale pricing is turned on. (Also Story 13.)

n_p03_18.text: 3.18 · Turn on separate Part Sale pricing. It starts as a copy of the work order prices.

n_p03_19.text: 3.19 · A matrix with its own Part Sale prices. Tread Plus Part Sale Matrix: same grid, its own rules. (Also Story 13.)

n_p03_20.text: 3.20 · Turn it off. "Turn off Part Sale pricing?" Cancel / Turn Off. (Also Story 13.)

n_p03_22.text: 3.22 · Result: Name, categories and the grid ready to fill; Cancel and Create Matrix in the page head, as on New Tier and New Category.

n_p03_23.text: 3.23 · Open Categories. Search and tick categories; one already on another matrix says so.

n_p03_24.text: 3.24 · Click Create Matrix with no name. Matrix name is a required field.

n_p03_25.text: 3.25 · Type a taken name and click Create Matrix. "A matrix called Stop 40 already exists."

n_p03_27.text: 3.27 · Result: A copy of its rules, ready to name.

n_p03_29.text: 3.29 · Result: "Delete Stop 40?" names the matrix. Its categories go to the General Matrix.

t_p03_3.text: New, duplicate or delete a matrix  (3.21–3.29)

n_p04_1.text: 4.1 · Hover the Cost Range info icon. Short tooltip explaining cost ranges.

n_p04_2.text: 4.2 · Hover a "Uses previous tier" cell. Names the previous tier by number and name: "Uses previous tier, 1 · Default." Through a chain it adds the tier whose rule prices it: "Uses previous tier, 2 · Tier 2. Priced by 1 · Default’s rule."

n_p04_3.text: 4.3 · A column that mixes rule types.

n_p04_4.text: 4.4 · Result: Tread Plus Default: + $45 up to $300, then 15% margin. In edit, the column's rule picker reads "Mixed rules" (4.15); the Categories list reads the same.

n_p04_6.text: 4.6 · Result: Every cell is editable. The bar shows "No changes yet", Cancel and Save.

n_p04_7.text: 4.7 · Type in a range. The ranges below that are empty or gray fill in gray with the same rule type and value. Gray values don't count as changes.

n_p04_8.text: 4.8 · Change range 2 to Markup % and type 45. Auto-fill follows the last range entered: range 3 and below follow range 2.

n_p04_9.text: 4.9 · A column's rule picker. Previous tier · Off default price (% Off, $ Off) · From cost (+ $, Markup %, Margin %). Picking one sets the whole column.

n_p04_10.text: 4.10 · Default's rule picker. Default can only use From cost types (+ $, Markup %, Margin %): no Previous tier, no % Off or $ Off.

n_p04_11.text: 4.11 · Pick % Off for Tier 5. % Off starts at 0% in every range.

n_p04_12.text: 4.12 · Pick "Previous tier" for Tier 2. The column shows the previous tier's values, muted; it prices the same as the tier before it.

n_p04_13.text: 4.13 · A From cost cell's symbol. The $ or % is a picker (chevron on the far right) so one range can use another From cost type. Alt+Down opens it.

n_p04_15.text: 4.15 · Result: The column header reads "Mixed rules"; cells spell out % markup / % margin.

n_p04_16.text: 4.16 · Same as previous tier, in edit.

n_p04_17.text: 4.17 · Result: The cells show the previous tier's values, muted, and can be typed over to give the tier its own copy.

n_p04_18.text: 4.18 · Type a bad value and click Save. Cells highlighted; the message names the problem; Save is blocked.

n_p04_19.text: 4.19 · Change a range end. Ranges are entered by their end; the next range starts a cent later.

n_p04_20.text: 4.20 · Click Add Range. A new last range; counts as one change.

n_p04_21.text: 4.21 · Click a range's delete. The range above takes its end; counts as one change.

n_p04_22.text: 4.22 · After a few edits. Changed cells are highlighted; the bar counts only cells someone edited.

n_p04_23.text: 4.23 · Click Cancel with changes. "Discard these changes?" Keep editing / Discard changes. (Also Story 19.)

n_p04_24.text: 4.24 · Change Default's rules. The confirm names every tier that prices from Default in this matrix. Dynamic 26 prices 3 categories, so the list joins "Change Prices in 3 Categories?"; a one-category matrix asks "Change Default's Prices?". (Also Story 3.)

n_p04_26.text: 4.26 · Result: The archived view: Default plus archived tiers, with a notice; only the archived columns can change.

n_p04_27.text: 4.27 · Hover Default's column in the archived view. "Default prices live parts, so it can't be changed in the archived view."

t_p04_2.text: Change Default's rules; the archived view  (4.24–4.27)

n_p05_1.text: 5.1 · Type a part cost in the Price Part Simulator. Every column shows the sell price and profit for that cost. Nothing is saved.

n_p05_2.text: 5.2 · A cost a tier sells below. The same triangle marks a below-cost price. (Also Story 15.)

n_p05_3.text: 5.3 · Type 0 as the part cost. The cost field shows an error and every column shows “—”. The same happens when the field is empty or not a number.

n_p05_4.text: 5.4 · Type a cost while editing the grid. The simulator uses the unsaved values in the grid.

n_p06_1.text: 6.1 · Today: the matrices list. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p06_2.text: 6.2 · Click the Matrices tab. Every matrix: Status, Categories, Work Order Matrix, Part Sale Matrix, and which tiers have their own rules.

n_p06_3.text: 6.3 · Hover the Tiers info icon. The Tiers column lists the numbers of the tiers with their own rules, or "All".

n_p06_4.text: 6.4 · Hover the tier numbers in the Tiers column. The numbers of the tiers with their own rules; their names on hover.

n_p06_5.text: 6.5 · Click the Status filter. Active and Inactive. Inactive = no category uses the matrix.

n_p06_7.text: 6.7 · Result: The chip turns blue with the selection.

n_p06_8.text: 6.8 · Hover an Inactive status. "No categories use this matrix."

n_p06_9.text: 6.9 · Search "tread". Search matches matrix and category names.

n_p06_10.text: 6.10 · A search with no match. The standard empty state with Clear Search.

n_p06_11.text: 6.11 · Click a matrix's three-dot menu. Duplicate, Delete.

n_p06_12.text: 6.12 · The General Matrix's menu. The General Matrix can't be deleted; hovering Delete says why.

n_p06_14.text: 6.14 · Result: "Audit Log: Matrices": every matrix's changes, deleted ones included. (Also Story 19.)

n_p07_1.text: 7.1 · Today: the Categories list. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p07_2.text: 7.2 · Today: Edit Category. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p07_3.text: 7.3 · Settings › Categories. Every category's pricing at a glance: its matrix, and each tier's rule in short.

n_p07_4.text: 7.4 · Hover a "Uses previous tier" cell. The hover lists each cost range on its own line; a "Uses previous tier" cell names the previous tier by number and name, and the tier whose rule prices it.

n_p07_5.text: 7.5 · Search "tire". Search matches category and matrix names.

n_p07_6.text: 7.6 · A search with no match. The standard empty state with Clear Search.

n_p07_8.text: 7.8 · Result: The category page: name, Tax Exempt, QuickBooks mapping, its matrix and that matrix's grid (read only), Edit. Delete is in the three-dot menu, left of New Matrix.

n_p07_9.text: 7.9 · A category whose matrix prices others. Edit is grayed. The info icon by the matrix name says "The Fluids 30 matrix also prices 1 other category: Oil."

n_p07_10.text: 7.10 · Hover the grayed Edit. "Can't edit here…" with a link to the matrix.

n_p07_11.text: 7.11 · Click "Go to the Fluids 30 matrix". The matrix opens ready to edit.

n_p07_12.text: 7.12 · Click New Matrix on a category's page.

n_p07_13.text: 7.13 · Result: The new matrix opens with this category already picked; the breadcrumb leads back to the category.

n_p08_1.text: 8.1 · Pick another matrix for the category. A category uses one matrix; the General Matrix when none is picked.

n_p08_3.text: 8.3 · Result: A system category: it can't be renamed, moved or deleted, and always uses the General Matrix.

n_p08_4.text: 8.4 · Rename Brakes to a taken name. "A category called tires already exists. Click away to keep Brakes."

n_p08_6.text: 8.6 · Result: Name (cursor in it), matrix, Cancel / Create Category.

n_p08_7.text: 8.7 · Click Create Category with no name. "Name is a required field."

n_p08_8.text: 8.8 · Type "Wheel Seals" and click Create Category.

n_p08_9.text: 8.9 · Result: Created on the General Matrix; the toast says so.

n_p08_10.text: 8.10 · Click Delete in the three-dot menu.

n_p08_11.text: 8.11 · Click Delete in the delete dialog.

n_p08_12.text: 8.12 · Result: The category is gone; its parts and past lines are in Uncategorized.

n_p09_1.text: 9.1 · Click the tier's Customers tab. Customers on this tier for Work Orders, Part Sales or both.

n_p09_2.text: 9.2 · Search a tier's Customers tab with no match. No customer matches.

n_p09_3.text: 9.3 · Open the Customers tab's channel filter. Filter the tier's customers: Work Orders and Part Sales, or Work Orders only.

n_p09_4.text: 9.4 · Click Manage Customers. Add Customers tab: every customer not on this tier, with the tiers they are on now.

n_p09_5.text: 9.5 · Hover the Add Customers tab. Each tab says what it does in a tooltip on its title; no message above the list. (Also Story 19.)

n_p09_6.text: 9.6 · Check two customers. The dark selection bar appears at the top, above the search, and shows how many are checked; you can still search while checking rows; each row can be Work Orders, Part Sales or both.

n_p09_7.text: 9.7 · Uncheck Part Sales on one row. That customer moves for Work Orders only.

n_p09_8.text: 9.8 · Uncheck both Work Orders and Part Sales on a row. "Pick Work Orders, Part Sales or both." The button is off.

n_p09_9.text: 9.9 · Click Select All. Every customer shown is checked.

n_p09_10.text: 9.10 · Uncheck Part Sales in the bar, then Select All.

n_p09_11.text: 9.11 · Result: Customers already on Tier 2 for the picked channel are skipped, and the footer says how many.

n_p09_12.text: 9.12 · Search customers. The list narrows; checks are kept.

n_p09_13.text: 9.13 · A search with no match. The standard empty state.

n_p09_15.text: 9.15 · Result: New work orders and Part Sales use Tier 2. Existing ones keep their prices and tier.

n_p09_16.text: 9.16 · Click the Remove Customers tab. Customers on this tier. Switching tabs clears the checks.

n_p09_18.text: 9.18 · Result: "Remove 1 Customer?" They go back to Default for the channels picked.

n_p09_20.text: 9.20 · Result: They are back on Default.

n_p09_21.text: 9.21 · An archived tier's Customers tab. No Manage Customers: an archived tier takes no customers. Reactivate Tier (the same as the menu's Reactivate) brings it back as the last tier.

n_p09_23.text: 9.23 · Result: No confirmation. It comes back as the last tier and can take customers.

n_p09_24.text: 9.24 · Remove tab of a tier with no customers. "No customer is on Tier 5 yet."

t_p09_0.text: A tier's customers and Manage Customers  (9.1–9.24)

n_p09_25.text: 9.25 · Today: the Customers list. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p09_26.text: 9.26 · Today: a customer's page. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p09_27.text: 9.27 · Today: Edit Customer. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p09_28.text: 9.28 · Customers. The customer list itself doesn't change.

n_p09_30.text: 9.30 · Result: The customer card's Pricing group: labor rate, shop supplies, tax, Work Order tier, Part Sales tier.

n_p09_31.text: 9.31 · Click Edit. Edit Customer: the two tier fields sit under Default Shop Supplies (shown only when the client has 2 or more tiers). Each tier field is a searchable picker.

n_p09_32.text: 9.32 · Click Work Order Tier and type 3. A searchable picker: active tiers by number. A number finds that tier first, then names that contain it; the current tier is ticked.

n_p09_35.text: 9.35 · Result: The card shows the new tier. Existing work orders and Part Sales keep their prices and tier.

n_p09_36.text: 9.36 · Edit the Counter Sale customer. Every walk-in sale uses this customer's tier.

n_p09_37.text: 9.37 · Edit Customer with only Default. With one tier (release day) the tier fields are hidden and the card shows no tier rows.

n_p09_38.text: 9.38 · Today: Edit Customer on a phone. Today (screenshot of production). Edit Customer on a phone stacks the same fields as desktop.

n_p09_39.text: 9.39 · On a phone: Edit Customer. A phone is narrower than 768 px. Edit Customer shows the same fields as desktop; the two tier fields sit under Default Shop Supplies, by number.

n_p09_40.text: 9.40 · On a phone: tap Work Order Tier. The same searchable picker as desktop: active tiers by number, a search for number or name, the current tier ticked.

n_p09_41.text: 9.41 · On a phone: pick 3 · Tier 3. The field shows the new tier. Save; existing work orders and Part Sales keep their prices and tier.

n_p10_1.text: 10.1 · Today: a work order. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p10_2.text: 10.2 · Today: Add Part, quick-add row. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p10_3.text: 10.3 · Today: cost fills the sell price. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p10_5.text: 10.5 · Result: Parts are priced by the work order's tier. Only a typed price carries an icon (gray).

n_p10_6.text: 10.6 · Quick Add a part with a cost. Its sell price fills in from the tier as soon as the cost is typed.

n_p10_8.text: 10.8 · Result: Priced by the work order's tier.

n_p10_9.text: 10.9 · Quick Add with a sell price of -5. "Sell price cannot be negative."

n_p10_11.text: 10.11 · Result: No rule prices it: $0.00, logged under the work order's tier.

t_p10_0.text: Pricing parts on a work order  (10.1–10.11)

n_p10_12.text: 10.12 · Click the Fixed Rules tab. Parts with a fixed sell price, read only in this release. A fixed price wins over tiers.

n_p11_1.text: 11.1 · Click a part. Edit Part Request: cost, sell price and margin.

n_p11_2.text: 11.2 · Type a sell price. A price that differs from the calculated one is Manual.

n_p11_3.text: 11.3 · Split Work Order (works as today). The new work order takes the customer's current tier; its parts are priced again. Typed, fixed and canned prices are kept.

n_p11_5.text: 11.5 · Result: The new work order, priced by the customer's current tier.

n_p11_6.text: 11.6 · Receive a part. The receive window is unchanged: it says nothing about tiers.

n_p11_7.text: 11.7 · Receive a tier-priced part at a new cost, then hover its price. Priced again by the tier recorded on the line at the received cost.

n_p12_1.text: 12.1 · Hover a price. Price details: tier, matrix, range and rule, cost, sell price, when, and where the part came from.

n_p12_2.text: 12.2 · Hover a part priced through Same as previous tier. Priced through Same as previous tier: the details name the tier it follows (Default), and where the part came from.

n_p12_3.text: 12.3 · Hover a typed price. "Price typed by hand": who typed it, the calculated price.

n_p12_4.text: 12.4 · Click the Parts tab. A Priced by column after Sell Price names the source in words.

n_p12_5.text: 12.5 · A line priced before tiers. "Priced before tiers": no Manual icon.

n_p12_6.text: 12.6 · The customer has moved tier since. "Priced by Default, Northway Haulers's tier when this work order was made. Northway Haulers is now on Tier 2."

n_p12_7.text: 12.7 · A canned line part on a Default work order. Saved price from the canned line; Priced by Default; the vendor and vendor bill number.

n_p12_8.text: 12.8 · A part on a fixed line total. Part of a fixed line total of $450.00 (parts $210.00).

n_p12_9.text: 12.9 · Hover a line priced for the previous customer. "Priced by … for Acme Freight." The line keeps its price.

n_p13_1.text: 13.1 · Today: a Part Sale. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p13_3.text: 13.3 · Result: Priced by the Part Sale's tier, from the Part Sale Matrix side when it is on.

n_p13_4.text: 13.4 · Hover a price. % Off Default: the Default price it came from.

n_p14_1.text: 14.1 · Today: Change Customer. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p14_2.text: 14.2 · Click the work order's three-dot menu. Change Customer, Split Work Order.

n_p14_3.text: 14.3 · Change Customer. "Parts already on the work order keep their prices, and new parts keep this work order's pricing."

n_p14_4.text: 14.4 · Pick a customer on another tier. "This work order keeps Tier 2 pricing. Default applies to new work orders, or split this one to use it."

n_p14_5.text: 14.5 · Change Customer on a Part Sale. "This Part Sale keeps Tier 4 pricing. Default applies to new Part Sales, or split this one to use it."

n_p14_6.text: 14.6 · Pick a customer on the same tier. No amber note.

n_p14_8.text: 14.8 · Result: A notice counts the lines priced for the previous customer. They keep their prices, and the work order keeps its tier.

n_p15_1.text: 15.1 · Hover the below-cost warning. The only grid warning: a triangle in a space kept beside every value, so nothing shifts.

n_p15_2.text: 15.2 · Type 95 in Tier 5 while editing. The below-cost warning appears as soon as the value makes a price fall below cost.

n_p20_1.text: 20.1 · Today: Sales By Customer, unchanged. Screenshot of production today; the screens after it show what changes.

n_p20_2.text: 20.2 · Reports › Sales by Tier. One row per pricing source. Columns: Parts Cost, Parts Invoiced (bold), Parts Credits, Parts Net, Parts Margin, Parts Margin %, % of Total. Date and Location chips are blue; the others are plain at All.

n_p20_3.text: 20.3 · Open a tier's row. Its customers, then their invoices.

n_p20_4.text: 20.4 · Open a customer's row. Their invoices and credits: linked numbers, and plain text where there is nothing to open.

n_p20_5.text: 20.5 · Open Priced By. Pick the rows to show; the chip turns blue with a selection. The list ends with Fixed price, Fixed line total, Manual and Before tiers.

n_p20_6.text: 20.6 · Open the Customer filter. Search and pick customers.

n_p20_7.text: 20.7 · Open the Category filter. Search and pick categories.

n_p20_8.text: 20.8 · Open the Location filter. Locations the user can see; always blue.

n_p20_9.text: 20.9 · Sales Type: Work Orders only. Part Sales / Work Orders. One picked turns the chip blue. A credit counts under its own Sales Type. Credits with no part lines (goodwill, overpayments, fees, write-offs) aren’t in these reports.

n_p20_10.text: 20.10 · Pick a custom range over one year. "Choose a date range of one year or less."

n_p20_11.text: 20.11 · Pick a range with no sales. "There are no results for selected date range".

n_p20_13.text: 20.13 · Result: First click on a number column puts the biggest on top (Parts Credits: the largest credit first); the second reverses; the third returns to the first-load order. Arrows show on hover and on the sorted column.

n_p20_14.text: 20.14 · Click the Columns icon. Show or hide Parts Cost, Parts Credits, Parts Net, Parts Margin, Parts Margin % and % of Total; Parts Invoiced always shows.

n_p20_15.text: 20.15 · Hide Parts Margin. The column is gone; the choice is kept for next time.

n_p20_16.text: 20.16 · Sales by Category. The same report by category; shared filters carry over.

n_p20_17.text: 20.17 · Open a category's row. Sales by Category: a category opens to its Priced By rows.

n_p20_18.text: 20.18 · Click Download. PDF up to 2,000 rows, CSV up to 50,000.

n_p20_20.text: 20.20 · Result: Prototype stand-in (see the info icon): the real menu item downloads the file. The file starts with the report title, the date range and every filter, written out, then Parts Credits and Parts Net beside Parts Invoiced. Copy is the primary button.

n_p20_23.text: 20.23 · Filters that match nothing. "No record matches these filters" with Clear All Filters.

t_p20_0.text: Sales by Tier and Sales by Category  (20.1–20.23)
